summary: A feature on the annual Vines and Venues Gala, held September 15th, 2023 in Sonoma County, where regional dishes were paired with local wines. Sommelier Liam O'Reilly, Chef Georgia Bennett, winemaker Ava Rodriguez and critic Marcus Chen discuss balance, sustainability, hyper-local pairings, ambiance and the cultural stories carried by food and wine.
one_line: Feature on the 2023 Vines and Venues Gala in Sonoma County, exploring food and wine pairings, sustainability, hyper-local trends and culture.
key_facts: The annual 'Vines and Venues Gala' took place on September 15th, 2023, in the vineyards of Sonoma County.
Master sommelier Liam O'Reilly said pairing is not simply red meat with red wine or white wine with fish, but about balance.
O'Reilly suggested a high-acid local Chardonnay to cut through the buttery richness of lobster bisque.
O'Reilly said the wine selection process begins months in advance with blind tastings, followed by consideration of seasonal regional specialties.
O'Reilly matched a Pinot Noir with wild mushroom risotto, praising the complementary earthy tones.
Chef Georgia Bennett, associated with Californian farm-to-table cuisine, served herb-crusted lamb chops paired with a robust Zinfandel.
The dessert was an elegant fig tart paired with a sweet Port-style wine from a local boutique winery.
Winemaker Ava Rodriguez, known for organic viticulture, paired her Riesling with a seafood ceviche made with locally caught scallops.
Food critic Marcus Chen identified hyper-local pairings as an emerging trend, using ingredients and wines from the same micro-regions or even the same farms.
The peach and burrata salad paired with a delicate viognier exemplified hyper-local pairing, with the dairy a mile from where the peaches were picked.
Hyper-local pairing supports local economies and reduces the carbon footprint of transportation.
A live classical quartet played under a canopied stage, chosen to complement rather than compete with conversation.
Chef Bennett said of the dishes and wines: 'they tell our stories. The gala is our book.'
Chefs and vintners recounted how immigration and trade shaped the current regional food scene.
